source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: Taurean Prince
injuries.short_comment: Prince (knee) underwent surgery to address lingering issues and has no timeline for a return, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.long_comment: With Detroit still without a return timetable for Prince after right knee surgery, he appears set for an extended absence well beyond Friday's tilt against Toronto. Prince hasn't been a significant part of the Pistons' rotation this season, so his continued absence is unlikely to create a major fantasy ripple effect.

injuries.name: Duncan Robinson
injuries.short_comment: Robinson will be re-evaluated in one week due to a left quadriceps strain, Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News reports.
injuries.long_comment: Robinson has gotten off to a strong start this season, though he's now expected to miss at least the next week after appearing in each of Detroit's first 12 regular-season games. The sharpshooter is averaging 17.4 points in 30.5 minutes per contest, and his absence will open up additional minutes for Kevin Huerter and Javonte Green.

injuries.name: Cade Cunningham
injuries.short_comment: Cunningham (knee) is probable for Tuesday's game against the Orlando.
injuries.long_comment: The superstar point guard has been managing lingering knee soreness as of late, but he's expected to fight through the issue Tuesday. Since the start of November,  Cunningham has averaged 25.6 points, 9.1 assists, 4.8 rebounds and 1.6 steals per contest covering nine appearances.

injuries.name: Jalen Duren
injuries.short_comment: Duren (hamstring) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
injuries.long_comment: Duren hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to a right hamstring strain, though he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Until the Pistons offer an update on the 23-year-old big man's progress, he can be considered week-to-week. Paul Reed will likely continue seeing increased minutes for as long as Duren is sidelined.

injuries.name: Ebuka Okorie
injuries.short_comment: Okorie (oblique) won't play Tuesday in Orlando.
injuries.long_comment: Okorie lacks a concrete timeline for a return due to an oblique injury. His ongoing absence carries little fantasy relevance moving forward.

injuries.name: Jonathan Isaac
injuries.short_comment: Isaac (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
injuries.long_comment: Isaac continues to deal with a knee injury that has kept him out of action for the entire 2026-27 season. He should continue to be considered week to week until the Magic offer an update on his recovery process.

injuries.name: Paolo Banchero
injuries.short_comment: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
injuries.long_comment: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

injuries.name: Izaiyah Nelson
injuries.short_comment: Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injuries.long_comment: Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injuries.name: Noah Penda
injuries.short_comment: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
injuries.long_comment: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.
